entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: 'or' between a float-valued and a histogram-valued operand does not support a %s-shaped float operand, which cerberus issue #2333 does not cover
entries.rationale: both callers reach this default switch arm only when RowShapeOf(floatNode) is neither SampleRowShape, GridWindowRowShape, nor ReducedWindowRowShape, i.e. HistogramRowShape or MixedRowShape — believed unreachable through any parseable query today, since the float side already failed isExpHistogramValuedShape before lower() is called on it. A defensive guard against a future histogram-aware float lowering silently mis-projecting through this path, not a live divergence. lowerMixedExpHistogramSetOp is the leaf case's own direct caller. shadowResolveMixedExpHistogramOperands (cerberus issue #2595) is a refactor of what used to be lowerSumOrAvgOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp's own inline call (cerberus issue #2453) into a shared helper histogram_native_mixed_or_aggregate.go's three aggregate families now all route through — sumOrAvgOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp (#2346), floatOnlyAggOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp, and countValuesOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp (both #2595) — none of which change how the float operand itself is lowered, so the same unreachability claim carries through unchanged for all three.

guard: default of switch shape over [case chplan.SampleRowShape, chplan.GridWindowRowShape, chplan.ReducedWindowRowShape; default]

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: 'bool' modifier is only allowed on comparison binary ops
entries.rationale: the parser rejects `bool` on non-comparison operators ("bool modifier can only be used on comparison operators"). Every one of this function's current callers obtains its `b`/`setOp` argument via [mixedExpHistogramSetOp] itself (directly, or by forwarding a value that function already returned), which requires `b.Op == parser.LOR` before matching — `or` is a set operator, never a comparison, so the parser can never have set ReturnBool on a BinaryExpr it produces with that Op. lowerMixedExpHistogramFamily is the root caller, reached from lowerHistogramNativeRoot's own dispatch (split out of lowerRoot's body purely to keep that function's golangci-lint maintainability-index score over the repo's floor) — it calls mixedExpHistogramSetOp(expr, ...) itself before forwarding the match. lowerArithmeticOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp, lowerComparisonOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp, lowerMulOrDivScaleOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp and lowerLabelCallOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp (cerberus issue #2449's wrapper families) each recognise their own wrapper shape by calling mixedExpHistogramSetOp on the operand themselves (see e.g. arithmeticOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp's own `inner, matched := mixedExpHistogramSetOp(vecSide, s, ctx)`), so the value they hand this function is always the freshly-matched inner `or`, never an outer node. lowerCountOrGroupOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp (count()/group(), cerberus issue #2595) and floatRowsOnlyOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp (the shared single-arg-math/round-to-nearest/clamp scaffolding, cerberus issues #2578/#2587) follow the identical pattern for their own shapes. lowerSortByLabelArgOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp and lowerTimestampOverMixedExpHistogramSetOp (sort_by_label()/sort_by_label_desc()/timestamp(), cerberus issue #2611) likewise. lowerVectorSetOpOperand (cerberus issue #2555, a mixed `or` nested under a further and/or/unless) and splitMixedExpHistogramSetOpByType (cerberus issue #2618, the histogram_value_fns.go/histogram_quantile.go/info() retry path, reached via the mixedOrHistogramValuedArg alias) both call mixedExpHistogramSetOp themselves immediately before forwarding its result here. lowerMixedOrSubqueryOuterFn (cerberus issue #2577) is the one caller that does not call mixedExpHistogramSetOp on a parser-produced node: it builds a SYNTHETIC `*parser.BinaryExpr{Op: parser.LOR}` from two arms matched inside a subquery's own inner expression — never seen by the parser, and the construction never sets ReturnBool, so it stays Go's zero value (false). Either way — a parser-produced or a synthetic node — no caller can ever hand this function a BinaryExpr with ReturnBool=true. Two further wrapper families handling vector-vector/vector-plain composition over a mixed `or` were callers of this function at one point; neither exists in the current source — that composition stays a deliberately unattempted shape (TestLower_ExpHistogram_MixedSetOpOr_ComparisonVectorVectorStillRejects pins the rejection).
